title: Exceptional tensor comparison for coefficients pulled from a field
statement:
Let $K$ be any field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $K$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $u:U\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ be a separated compactifiable finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary small etale derived categories, derived tensor, and compact support [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-kun-derived-tensor, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Let $u^!$ be the exceptional right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The canonical tensor map is a natural isomorphism for every $N\in D^+(K_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$:
$$T_u(\Lambda,N):u^!\Lambda\otimes_\Lambda^Lu^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}u^!N.$$
There is no perfectness, constructibility, or finite cohomological dimension assumption on $N$ or $K$; $U$ need not be regular or smooth.

For any compactifiable map $h:X\to Y$ between Noetherian schemes, $T_h(P,Q):h^!P\otimes^Lh^*Q\to h^!(P\otimes^LQ)$ denotes the transpose of inverse compact-support projection followed by $\epsilon_h(P)\otimes1_Q$. The preceding isomorphism is this particular map, with $P=\Lambda$. These maps are natural, restrict to source and target opens, and satisfy for composable $X\xrightarrow hY\xrightarrow kZ$
$$T_{kh}(P,Q)=h^!T_k(P,Q)\circ T_h(k^!P,k^*Q)$$
after identifying $(kh)^!=h^!k^!$ and $(kh)^*=h^*k^*$. This identity is an identity of maps wherever the displayed derived tensors are defined; it does not assert that $T_h$ is invertible for arbitrary sheaves on $Y$. The field-base isomorphism and these identities also hold on restrictions to localizations of $U$, using [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]; hence for essentially finite-type maps between spectra of fields.

proof.text:
Write $F_h=Rh_!$, $G_h=h^!$, and $\epsilon_h:F_hG_h\to1$. The compact-support projection $\Pi_h:F_h(A\otimes^Lh^*Q)\to F_hA\otimes^LQ$ is invertible on the whole ordinary derived categories: on a compactification $h=rj$, combine the inverse open-extension tensor comparison with the proper projection isomorphism [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor, lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. Compactification independence and composition are those of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Using the ambient adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], define $T_h(P,Q)$ as the unique adjunct of
$$F_h(G_hP\otimes^Lh^*Q)\xrightarrow{\Pi_h}F_hG_hP\otimes^LQ\xrightarrow{\epsilon_h(P)\otimes1}P\otimes^LQ.$$
This fixes the map, including its direction; all these operations are available without a Tor hypothesis.

proof.text:
For composable $h,k$, use $F_{kh}=F_kF_h$ and the right-adjoint identification $G_{kh}=G_hG_k$. The composite counit is $\epsilon_k\circ F_k\epsilon_hG_k$, by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. The inverse form of [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] identifies the composite projection $\Pi_{kh}$ with $\Pi_k\circ F_k\Pi_h$. Consequently the adjunct of the proposed right-hand side is, writing $Q'=k^*Q$,
$$F_kF_h(G_hG_kP\otimes h^*Q')\xrightarrow{F_k\Pi_h}F_k(F_hG_hG_kP\otimes Q')\xrightarrow{F_k(\epsilon_h(G_kP)\otimes1)}F_k(G_kP\otimes Q')\xrightarrow{\Pi_k}F_kG_kP\otimes Q\xrightarrow{\epsilon_k(P)\otimes1}P\otimes Q.$$
Naturality of $\Pi_k$ moves $F_k\epsilon_h$ through that projection, making this exactly the composite counit after $\Pi_{kh}$. Adjunction's injectivity therefore proves $T_{kh}=h^!T_k\circ T_h$. This uses equality of the specified projections and counits, rather than equality on a generating class.

proof.text: Naturality in $P,Q$ follows by taking adjuncts of the natural composite in Step 1. For an open immersion $a$, exact extension by zero is left adjoint to $a^*$, and $a^*h^!=(ha)^!$ [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. In Step 1 the open-extension projection restricts to the identity on the open; hence its transpose identifies $T_a$ with the ordinary restriction/tensor isomorphism. Step 2 now gives restriction of $T_h$ to source opens. For a target open $b:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$, put $X'=X\times_YY'$ and $a:X'\hookrightarrow X$, $h':X'\to Y'$. The equality $ha=bh'$ and exceptional transitivity give $a^*h^!=h'^!b^*$. Apply Step 2 to both factorizations: their $T$ maps agree by the common composite and the open $T$ identifications. This proves target-open compatibility too. Isomorphisms can be checked on a source-open cover, by exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks and the cohomology criterion, also for unbounded tensors.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-affine-chart-factorization-gluing] to $u$. By Step 3 it suffices on each chart to consider $u=pi$ with $i:U\hookrightarrow T=\mathbf A^m_K$ closed and $p:T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ smooth of pure relative dimension $m$. The charts, their open complements and their changes of field are Noetherian; an open of a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The required compactifications exist by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Fields are excellent and so are their finite-type algebras [lem-exc-fields-excellent, lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]; this is the excellence required by the supported calculus in Step 10. The prime-power smooth orientation [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality] applies to $p$: it is smooth, separated, of finite type and of pure relative dimension $m$ between Noetherian schemes with $\ell$ invertible, and compactifiable by Nagata; no excellence, perfectness or characteristic hypothesis is needed. It gives the orientation $\gamma_{p,n}:\Lambda_T(m)[2m]\xrightarrow{\sim}p^!\Lambda$, and for every $N\in D^+(K_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ the orientation followed by the counit-defined exceptional tensor map $T_p(\Lambda,N)$ is an isomorphism $p^*N(m)[2m]\xrightarrow{\sim}p^!N$. No regularity of the closed subscheme $U$ is required.

source.place: Theorem 7.19 (affine-space reduction and diagonal/deformation smooth purity); local factorization as in Gabber XVII, proof after Lemma 4.4.1

proof.text:
For the open complement $j:V=T\setminus U\hookrightarrow T$, or its base change to any field extension of $K$, [lem-kun-0f10] gives finite relative cohomological dimension; no bound for $\operatorname{cd}(K)$ is needed. The map $j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [lem-kun-0f11] says $Rj_*$ preserves arbitrary coproducts. Fix any $E\in D(V_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Consider, for $M\in D(\Lambda)$, the canonical projection
$$\alpha_M:(Rj_*E)\otimes^L M_T\longrightarrow Rj_*(E\otimes^LM_V).$$
Here $M_S$ is the termwise constant complex. Constant sheafification is exact and preserves sums (equivalently it is inverse image from the point topos), and constant complexes restrict as in [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Both functors of $M$ preserve coproducts by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-direct-sums] and the preceding bound. They are exact and $\alpha$ respects shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. The isomorphism locus contains $\Lambda[r]$ for every $r$ because $\alpha_\Lambda=1$; it is closed under coproducts, triangles by two-out-of-three, and retracts. By [lem-pc-derived-module-free-generation] it is all of $D(\Lambda)$. Thus this particular projection is invertible even for unbounded $M$ and modules of infinite projective dimension.

proof.text: For any $B\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, tensor the closed-support triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] by $M_T$. Compare it with the support triangle of $B\otimes^LM_T$. The middle map is the identity, and the third map is $\alpha_M$ of Step 5 for $E=j^*B$, using [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. The first map is $i_*T_i(B,M_T)$ after the proper projection identification for $i$ [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. Indeed its composite with the support counit is $\epsilon_i(B)\otimes1$; this is the defining adjoint equation of Step 1. Construct the diagram on the mapping-fibre model of the unit $B\to Rj_*j^*B$; tensor exactness and naturality of the projection give its connecting square as well. Thus two-out-of-three gives an isomorphism on the first vertex [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. Closed direct image has left inverse $i^{-1}$ [lem-kun-04ca], hence reflects isomorphisms, so $T_i(B,M_T)$ is invertible. This is an ordinary support-triangle argument and assumes neither purity nor regularity of $i$.

proof.text:
Let $\Omega=K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and write $g:T_\Omega\to T$, $g_U:U_\Omega\to U$. The map $g$ is affine locally ind-etale: $\Omega$ is the filtered union of its finite separable subextensions, each finite etale over $K$, and tensoring their algebras with an affine coordinate ring gives their base changes. Both source and target schemes are Noetherian finite-type schemes over their respective fields. Therefore [lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change] gives
$$g_U^*i^!B\cong i_\Omega^!g^*B\qquad(B\in D^+(T,\Lambda)).$$
It identifies the supported counits. Together with the monoidal inverse image comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], it identifies the pullback of $T_i(B,Q)$ with $T_{i_\Omega}(g^*B,g^*Q)$ whenever $B,Q,B\otimes^LQ$ are bounded below: transpose both maps after closed direct image; each is the pulled-back supported counit tensored with $1_{g^*Q}$. In this calculation the closed projection has the canonical stalk description (tensor on $U_\Omega$, zero off it), so its pullback is the same projection. This proves compatibility of the actual maps, not just their objects. We shall apply it only with $B=p^!\Lambda=\Lambda_T(m)[2m]$ and $Q=p^*N$; all three required inputs are bounded below.

source.place: Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle); ind-etale supported comparison and its counit normalization

proof.text: Over the separably closed field $\Omega$, [lem-exc-etale-sheaves-gsets-point] has trivial Galois group. Its equivalence with sets respects products and algebraic operations, hence identifies $\Lambda$-module sheaves with $\Lambda$-modules. This is an exact equivalence of abelian categories and, termwise, of their derived categories. Thus $N|_\Omega$ is the constant complex of some $M\in D^+(\Lambda)$, and $g^*p^*N=M_{T_\Omega}$ by [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Step 6 applies to $g^*B$ and this arbitrary $M$. By Step 7 the pullback of $T_i(p^!\Lambda,p^*N)$ is invertible. Conservativity of separable-closure pullback [lem-kun-sep-closure-conservative] makes $T_i(p^!\Lambda,p^*N)$ itself invertible over $K$. This argument trivializes coefficients after conservative base change; it does not presume that the original $N$ is lisse, constructible, or perfect.

source.place: Tag 03QT (theorem-equivalence-sheaves-point); separable-closure conservativity and the closed-support computation

proof.text:
Apply Step 2 with $h=i$, $k=p$, $P=\Lambda$, $Q=N$. It gives precisely
$$T_u(\Lambda,N)=i^!T_p(\Lambda,N)\circ T_i(p^!\Lambda,p^*N).$$
The second factor is invertible by Step 8. The first is invertible because $N\in D^+$: by [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality] the composite of $\gamma_{p,n}\otimes1:p^*N(m)[2m]\to p^!\Lambda\otimes^Lp^*N$ with $T_p(\Lambda,N)$ is an isomorphism, and $\gamma_{p,n}\otimes1$ is one, so $T_p(\Lambda,N)$ is invertible. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so the composite is invertible. Step 3 then gives invertibility on all of $U$. The tensor was computed in the ambient unbounded category throughout; the resulting isomorphism places it in $D^+$, because the right adjoint on a chart is $i^!p^!$, with $p^!$ a shift-twist and $i^!$ the right derived supported functor. Thus the assertion is meaningful for every stated bounded-below $N$, even if its derived tensor with an arbitrary unrelated object would be unbounded below.

source.place: Theorem 7.19 and Lecture V counit-defined tensor comparison; agent combination with the closed-support calculation

proof.text: Finally use the model restrictions of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]; its schemes are excellent by Step 4 [lem-exc-fields-excellent, lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. A localization of the source pulls the already invertible $T_u(\Lambda,N)$ back by exact monoidal inverse image [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], so it remains invertible. The cited model-restriction statement gives independence of the finite-type model, pseudofunctorial composition, and compatibility with these counit-defined tensor maps. Consequently the composition equation of Step 2 and the open equations of Step 3 restrict to the localized maps, in particular to essentially finite-type maps between spectra of fields. No compact-support right adjoint for a non-finite-type map is being asserted. The empty source yields the unique isomorphism of zero objects; $m=0$ is included by the identity affine-space projection. A singular or nonreduced source is covered by exactly the same closed-support argument, which made no regular-immersion hypothesis.
